subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Caffeine and Physical Performance
description: A 60-second lesson on Caffeine and Physical Performance.

hook.text: Caffeine is the most widely used legal performance enhancer in sports. Nearly every elite athlete uses it.

buildup.text: It reduces perceived exertion—hard exercise feels easier—and mobilizes fatty acids for fuel, sparing glycogen.

discovery.text: 3–6 mg/kg body weight improves endurance by 2–4%, strength by 3–5%, and sprint performance measurably.

twist.text: The World Anti-Doping Agency removed caffeine from its banned list in 2004. It's simply too common to prohibit.

climax.text: Strategic caffeine timing—60 minutes before competition—is now standard in professional sports coaching.

punchline.text: Legal, effective, universal. Caffeine is sports' open secret.

quiz.question: How does caffeine improve endurance performance?
options: It reduces perceived exertion and mobilizes fatty acids for fuel
